channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: British Pound: Resilient growth supports more BoE hikes - Commerzbank
item.description: Volkmar Baur at Commerzbank highlights the UK economy’s resilient growth, with upward revisions to GDP and solid monthly data. With inflation still sticky and core inflation at 2.6%, he now expects the Bank of England to hike rates in November and again in February to 4.25%.

item.title: Euro picks up against British Pound with French debt, Oil prices still weighing
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trims losses against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, as the bond rout eased, allowing for a mild risk appetite during the Asian session.

item.title: Euro: Recovery capped by resistance against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that EUR/USD has bounced off recent lows near 1.1164 but downside momentum remains lacklustre. The Euro’s recovery is seen as constrained within 1.1190–1.1240 intraday, while the broader 1–3 week view still allows for a test of 1.1145 as long as strong resistance at 1.1265 holds and the oversold downtrend phase persists.

item.title: WTI declines to near $89.50 as Trump rules out attacks on Iran before midterm elections
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $89.65 during the early European trading hours on Friday. WTI declines after US President Donald Trump said Washington would not attack Iran before November’s midterm elections.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Risk-on sentiment lends support
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is up 0.17% at around 1.3250 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday. The GBP/USD pair gains as a pullback in United States (US) Treasury Yields after a juggernaut rally has lifted market sentiment.

item.title: Indian Rupee gets relief from pullback in US bond yields
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens slightly higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The USD/INR pair ticks lower to near 96.55, but is still close to its all-time high of 97.00. The Indian currency gets a much-needed reprieve from a corrective move in United States (US) Treasury Yields.

item.title: Gold hits fresh weekly top, eyes $4,200 as USD weakens further amid softer bond yields
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) gains positive traction for the second straight day on Friday, extending this week's recovery from a two-month low.

item.title: Asian Stocks struggle as OpenAI revenue miss hits AI sector, trade concerns loom
item.description: Asian stocks struggled on Friday following an overnight selloff in US tech shares, as concerns over OpenAI’s revenue outlook weighed heavily on the broader artificial intelligence sector.

item.title: Swiss Franc remains on front foot as USD slips further amid softer bond yields
item.description: The USD/CHF pair attracts sellers for the second straight day on Friday, extending the previous day's retracement slide from the vicinity of mid-0.8300s, or a one-week high.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Strengthens above 110.00, but remains bearish below 100-day SMA
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross trades in positive territory around 110.30, snapping the two-day losing streak during the early European trading hours. Cautious rhetoric from Japanese policymakers weighs on the Japanese Yen (JPY) against the Australian Dollar (AUD).

item.title: China set to resume fuel exports in October following brief suspension — Reuters
item.description: China is set to resume refined fuel exports in October following a temporary suspension during the Golden Week holiday, Reuters reported on Friday. This move aims to help ease tight global diesel, gasoline and jet ‌fuel markets.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Friday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Holds gains near 1.1230 on softer USD; bearish bias persists
item.description: The EUR/USD pair attracts buyers for the second straight day, rising to the 1.1225-1.1230 area during the Asian session on Friday amid a weak US Dollar (USD). Spot prices, however, remain confined within a range held since the beginning of this month, warranting some caution for bulls.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Tests 177.50 barrier near nine-day EMA
item.description: EUR/JPY gains ground for the second consecutive day, trading around 177.40 during Asian hours on Friday. Technical analysis of the daily chart shows that the currency cross is moving downward within the descending channel pattern, suggesting a persistent bearish bias.

item.title: United States Dollar Index weakens further amid correction in US bond yields
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) extends its decline against its major peers on Friday as United States (US) Treasury Yields correct after failing to extend the rally.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises above $60.00 as inflation fears ease
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) gains ground after three days of losses, trading around $60.10 per troy ounce during Asian hours on Friday. Non-yielding Silver gains support as a decline in oil prices eases inflationary concerns and Fed rate hike expectations.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar strengthens above 0.5600 amid softer US Dollar, easing yields
item.description: The NZD/USD pair gains traction to near 0.5615 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. The US Dollar (USD) weakens against the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) amid easing Treasury bond yields. Traders weigh lingering inflation concerns and the outlook for Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rates.

item.title: Canadian Dollar strengthens as risk-on mood weighs on US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 1.4210 during Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles for firm direction as softer USD limits intraday slide
item.description: The USD/JPY pair struggles to capitalize on a modest Asian session uptick on Friday, now trading near the lower end of its daily range, below the 158.00 mark amid a broadly weaker US Dollar (USD).

item.title: British Pound edges higher to near 1.3250, renewed UK fiscal concerns in focus
item.description: The GBP/USD pair gathers strength to around 1.3240 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. The US Dollar (USD) softens against the British Pound (GBP) following comments from Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama says DOGE Initiative to drive growth and fiscal sustainability under Takaichi
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that the country's doge initiative is key for the Sanae Takaichi administration to pursue budget promoting growth while maintaining fiscal sustainability, Reuters reported.

item.title: Australian Dollar edges higher amid modest USD weakness; upside potential seem limited
item.description: The AUD/USD pair edges higher during the Asian session on Friday, looking to build on the overnight bounce from the lower boundary of the weekly range amid a softer US Dollar (USD). Spot prices, however, lack bullish conviction and currently trade above mid-0.6900s, up just over 0.10% for the day.

item.title: WTI slips below $90.50 as Trump signals no pre-election strike on Iran
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price declines after posting nearly 2.5% gains in the previous day, trading around $90.30 per barrel during Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7330 vs. 6.7367 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Friday at 6.7330 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7367 and 6.7973 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro holds gains above 1.1200 despite France's fiscal worries
item.description: The EUR/USD pair holds positive ground near 1.1215 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. Nonetheless, the potential upside for the major pair might be limited amid fears of France’s debt crisis. The Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index data for October is due later on Friday.

item.title: US draws up new plan for 3 days of Iran strikes
item.description: US President Donald Trump has ordered plans to be drawn up for options of returning to fighting against Iran, even as he said earlier that strikes would not restart before the midterm elections on November 3, the New York Times reported on Thursday.

item.title: Gold gains ground to near $4,150 as traders weigh Fed rate path
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) edges higher to around $4,140 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal rebounds from a two-month low as traders assess the outlook for energy prices and weighed the Federal Reserve's (Fed) uncertain interest-rate path.

item.title: Yen gains as Trump rules out Iran strikes before the midterms
item.description: The 10-year Treasury yield ended near 5.22% after President Trump said on Truth Social that the US won't attack Iran before the midterm elections. It had touched its highest since 2002 on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar slides as AI sell-off rattles Wall Street
item.description: The Aussie Dollar dives 0.11% on Thursday as the US Dollar retreats from monthly highs, with safe-haven flows shifting from the Greenback to the Japanese Yen and the Swiss Franc amid losses on Wall Street and US yields. The AUD/USD trades at 0.6960 at the time of writing.

item.title: Pound holds its floor as BoE member Greene presses for a hike
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) external member Greene said in Cape Town that it's dangerous to assume markets will do the BoE's work for it, and that UK pay awards look set for about 3.5% next year. She has voted for a hike at each of the last three meetings.
